title: Cross-plan ownership canvas and early-warning lanes for roadmap dependencies
creator: Anika Rao
description:
Problem: We currently lack a consistent, lightweight artifact that clarifies who owns each dependency across plans (product, infra, design, security) and surfaces imminent blockers early. This causes late escalations, hidden rework during handoffs, and uneven resource allocation against OKRs.

Proposal: Create a cross-plan "Ownership Canvas" that sits alongside each initiative in the roadmap and a complementary set of "Early-Warning Lanes" (EWL) which are signals + thresholds that auto-badge tickets when a dependency is at-risk. The artifact will be: 1) a one-page canvas describing the dependent capability, owner(s), SLA/target, interface contract, rollback/fallback, and acceptance gate; 2) an EWL config stored as a simple ruleset (latency of progress, unresolved blockers > X days, test/regression failure) that power alerts and a readiness score.

Why this approach: The canvas lowers coordination overhead (single source to answer who/what/when), the EWL provides predictable early signals so PMs and Eng leads can re-prioritize before endgame. We prioritize low-friction adoption: 1) use existing Linear fields + a short template; 2) expose canvas in Console roadmap views; 3) start with manual curation for top 10 initiatives, then automate EWL ingestion from CI/issue metrics.

Scope: Pilot for Q2 initiatives across Product, Eng, Design, Security, and Infra. Deliverables: canvas template (Confluence & Figma), EWL ruleset prototype (spreadsheet + config), lightweight integration to Console roadmap view (read-only tile), and a runbook for owners.
acceptance_criteria: Canvas template created and reviewed by PM, Eng, Design, Security (link in attachments)
EWL prototype ruleset implemented in spreadsheet and validated against last quarter's initiatives
Top 10 initiatives have canvas filled and owner confirmed
Readiness score and EWL badges show up in the Console roadmap read-only tile for pilot initiatives
Runbook published with escalation paths and on-call contact mapping
success_metrics: Reduction in endgame escalations tied to dependency surprises by 40% vs baseline quarter
Average time between first EWL badge and blocker resolution >= 3 days (earlier detection)
>80% of pilot owners report canvas reduced coordination meetings for the initiative
Automated ingestion accuracy for EWL signals >= 75% on retrospective sample
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (Week 0-3): Build canvas template, EWL spreadsheet, and review with stakeholders (PM, Eng leads, Design, Security, Infra). Phase 2 (Week 4-6): Manual populate top-10 initiatives, surface read-only tile in Console for pilot teams, collect feedback. Phase 3 (Week 7-12): Automate EWL ingestion from issue metadata and CI, iterate rules, expand to full OKR set. Fall-through: if automation proves noisy, keep manual gating and focus on enforcement via quarterly release checkpoints.
